title: Dipole-wall collision: vorticity of the control and of the two micropolar runs at four times
caption: Normal collision of a dipole with the no-slip wall x = W (thick line; Clercx & Bruneau 2006, box [-W, W]^2, Re = U W / nu_inf = 625; the upper half 0.4 <= x / W <= 1, 0 <= y / W <= 0.6 is shown, the flow being symmetric). Vorticity omega W / U on one colour scale (saturated at +-300; contours at +-10, +-30, +-50 as in the paper's figures) at t U / W = 0.35, 0.45, 0.6, 0.7 (columns): before and after the first and the second collision (enstrophy peaks of the control at t = 0.372 and 0.649). Rows: (a-d) the Newtonian control of viscosity mu_inf; (e-h) the micropolar fluid, K = 3, l = W / 100 (10 dx); (i-l) the micropolar fluid, l = W / 50 (20 dx); (m-p) w - omega / 2 of l = W / 50 (saturated at +-60): the micro-rotation layer on the wall and where it is shed. w = 0 on every wall, w = omega / 2 at t = 0. dx = W / 1000 (4 million fluid particles), h = 5 dx; the fields are the particle velocities on a grid of one spacing (quadratic B-spline, no-slip reflection at the wall), the vorticity by central differences.
